{{Quote|The Praji legacy runs the gamut of the sentient experience. Their name fades in and out of the history files, leaving gaps of whole centuries, but always reappears.|[[Doctor/Legends|Dr]] [[Gabrel Treon]], "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]," [[Byblos Journal of Historical Science]]|<ref name="Tinker" />}}
'''House Praji''' was a wealthy [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] family originally from [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]]. The Prajii were one of the original [[Core Founder/Legends|signatories]] of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], and over the twenty-five thousand years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] history, produced numerous [[Republic Military/Legends|military]] [[Officer/Legends|officers]], [[Politics/Legends|politicians]], [[Bank/Legends|financiers]], and several [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]. Throughout their history, they maintained a pronounced rivalry with [[House Vahali/Legends|House Vahali]], another noble house of Kaikielius. From [[4800 BBY]], the Prajii were established at the [[Praji Estate]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where they established influence in the [[Bank of the Core/Legends|Bank of the Core]], and in the lead-up to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Coruscant Ministry of Ingress/Legends|Coruscant Ministry of Ingress]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], they re-established themselves on Kaikielius at the expense of their ancient rivals, the Vahalii, from where they continued their influence on galactic politics despite the destruction of the Praji holdings on Coruscant during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].

==History==
===Early history===
The earliest known progenitor of the Prajii was [[Tyler Sapius Praji]], the governor of the pastoral [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Kaikielius/Legends|Kaikielius]]. Tyler Praji was one of the signatories of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]], the founding document of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], in [[25,053 BBY]]. On Kaikielius, House Praji was one of the [[Triad (Great Houses)|Triad]], the three most powerful of the [[Great House]]s of the planet's aristocracy. Together, the Triad had a powerful voice on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], though perhaps owing to Tyler Praji's role in the foundation of the Republic, House Praji had the greatest ties to the capital.<ref name="Tinker" />

House Praji maintained an ancient rivalry with the other houses of the Triad, [[House Vahali/Legends|House Vahali]] and [[House Juoni]], which was believed to date from the colonization of Kaikielius. However, House Juoni was destroyed during the [[First Alsakan Conflict]] of [[17,000 BBY]] after it backed [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] while its rivals supported Coruscant, leaving Kaikielius to the Prajii and Vahalii. For another five thousand years, the Prajii's power grew at home even as Kaikielius' galactic influence dwindled. In [[11,660 BBY]], during the [[Twelfth Pius Dea Crusade]], [[Commodore/Legends|Commodore]] [[Daymont Praji|Daymont "Veracity" Praji]] commanded a fleet in the [[Pius Dea]]-dominated [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]]. Daymont Praji led the [[Bombardment of Zarracina III|bombardment]] of [[Zarracina III]] after the native [[Zarracine]]s refused to accept annexation and conversion to Pius Dea rule.<ref name="Tinker" />

===Exodus to Coruscant===
From [[11,000 BBY]], Kaikielius rivalled with [[Koros]] for influence in the Core Worlds, but infighting in the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros system]], and between the Great Houses on Kaikielius, prevented either from gaining an advantage. In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], however, the nine planets of the Koros system were [[Unification Wars (Koros)/Legends|unified]] by [[Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]], putting Kaikielius at an extreme disadvantage. The Prajii's homeworld underwent rapid urbanisation and industrialisation in a desperate attempt to keep up with Koros, resulting in the development of the infamous "[[Ring-city|ring-cities]]," which were soon abandoned to poverty and crime. Fast losing money on Kaikielius, House Praji moved much of its operations to Coruscant, and after suffering badly during the [[Quake Years]] around [[4800 BBY]], abandoned the planet for good, leaving rule of the increasingly-ungovernable planet to [[House Vahali/Legends|House Vahali]].<ref name="Tinker" />

House Praji ceased to exist as a formal entity, and having sold their ancestral holdings on Kaikielius at a loss, the family had no real estate except on Coruscant. It would not recover economically for centuries, with many scions of the family falling into obscurity owing to financial mismanagement. However, the Prajii increased their informal influence by gaining election to high office, and eventually became the majority shareholders of the [[Bank of the Core/Legends|Bank of the Core]]. By [[4225 BBY]], the Prajii once again held great influence on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. [[Emppu Praji-Barck]] served as a Republic [[Minister of State]] for sixty years, while the family had produced several [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] by marrying sons to daughters of the [[Draay family]]. [[Derrica Praji]] was one of these Jedi around this time, training under [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Vandar Tokare]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] before, to the fury of his relatives, becoming part of a joint Republic-Jedi expedition to Kaikielius.<ref name="Tinker" />

Emppu Praji-Barck, Derrica's great-aunt, had continually filibustered [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] debates on intervention in the [[Kaikielius system/Legends|Kaikielius system]]: all government positions were now filled by the Vahalii, but the planet was ''de facto'' controlled by criminals, [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], and [[Hutt/Legends|Hut]] [[Kajidic/Legends|''kajidics'']], and the Prajii were content to let their rivals destroy themselves before they moved back in to pick up the pieces. However, the Republic had discovered that the [[Odominic]] ''kajidic'' had been supplying weapons to both sides in the war between gangs and [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] on Kaikielius. Now a matter of Republic security rather than one of law enforcement, the planet's criminal elements were ousted in the [[Kaikieli Reconquista]]. During the course of the Reconquista, Derrica Praji discovered evidence in the capital [[Kesipli]] that
Emppu Praji-Barck had committed sedition in urging the Odominic to supply both sides of the gang war. For the sake of his family, Derrica chose to destroy the evidence, though House Praji's objective of seizing sole power on Kaikielius had come to naught. Derrica cut all contact with his family in the aftermath and returned to Ossus to be named [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]].<ref name="Tinker" />

===Plutocrats===
Despite the failure of their strategy on Kaikielius, the Prajii expansion continued apace from [[4225 BBY]] as they accepted Coruscant as their home and increased their influence in the [[Bank of the Core/Legends|Bank of the Core]]. Following the abolition of the [[Aurodium/Legends|aurodium standard]] the Bank of the Core became a key backer of the [[Republic Treasury Reserve]], and for millennia a Praji would always sit on the BOTC Executive Board. Over the centuries, the Prajii increased their ties with the rest of the patrician class through intermarriage: centuries before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[Lithio Motti]] married a Praji heiress to secure startup capital for his [[megonite moss]]-mining enterprise on [[Phelarion/Legends|Phelarion]]. The [[Motti family]] would dominate that industry for centuries, and during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], one of their number, [[Thalassa Tarkin|Thalassa Motti]], even married into the [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] [[Tarkin family/Legends|Tarkins]].<ref name="Tinker" />

The Prajii's financial influence resulted in a political scandal sometime prior to [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]]: [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Vaila Pecivas]] attempted to appoint [[Jideon Praji]] as her [[Minister of Finance (Republic)|Minister of Finance]]. However, since Jideon was also [[Bank of the Core Executive Board Chair|Executive Board Chair]] of the Bank of the Core, the appointment was seen to create a conflict of interest, and [[holomedia]] uproar and a [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] inquiry forced him to resign after just days in the post.<ref name="Tinker" />

By the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Prajii had grown to such wealth that the [[Praji Estate]], near the [[Bank of the Core Plaza]] in Coruscant's [[Financial District (Coruscant)/Legends|Financial District]], dwarfed provincial capitals on [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. Thousands of offices for the family's employees encircled a park large enough to land a [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]], which was maintained by its own chapter house of [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]] gardeners.<ref name="Tinker" />

===The Rise of the Empire===
[[File:TannonPraji.jpg|thumb|right|150px|[[Tannon Praji/Legends|Tannon Praji]], [[First Minister (Coruscant Ministry of Ingress)/Legends|First Minister]] of the [[Coruscant Ministry of Ingress/Legends|Coruscant Ministry of Ingress]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].]]
By the [[100 BBY/Legends|last century]] of the Galactic Republic, House Praji's patriarch was [[Tannon Praji/Legends|Tannon Praji]]. Tannon was a great patron of the arts and built his own fortune separate to House Praji's while continuing the investment in the Bank of the Core. When [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] became [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], one of his first appointments was to make Tannon [[Second Minister/Legends|Second Minister]] of the [[Coruscant Ministry of Ingress/Legends|Coruscant Ministry of Ingress]] under [[First Minister (Coruscant Ministry of Ingress)/Legends|First Minister]] [[Zelebitha Effhod]]. Both were soon forced to deal with the pressures of large numbers of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]] displaced by the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], and Tannon took the decision to close [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] borders to new immigrants indefinitely. Tannon soon became First Minister after Effhod's death from [[Quannot's Syndrome]] just as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] began.<ref name="Tinker" />

Tannon was troubled by the decisions he had to make as the war progressed, though the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]] cast him as an uncaring elitist, particularly after he denounced the destruction of art treasures in the [[Museum of Light]] on [[Tandis Four]] as an atrocity. As First Minister he oversaw efforts directed by [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic/Legends|COMPOR]] to deport ''en masse'' [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]], [[Gossam/Legends|Gossam]], and other species whose [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]] had sided with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. This led him to be the target of numerous assassination attempts, once by Aqualish, and another by [[Zarracine]]s. Consequently, he took the Bank of the Core's [[Special Agent/Legends|Special Agent]] [[Ottegru Grey]], who had already foiled a number of Separatist attempts to destabilise the bank, as a bodyguard.<ref name="Tinker" />

Other significant Prajii during the Clone Wars were Tannon's brother [[Griff Praji|Griff]], whose son [[Nahdonnis Praji|Nahdonnis]] would become a prominent [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] officer, and Tannon's wife [[Maree Praji|Maree]] and their daughter [[Onnelly Praji|Onnelly]]. While many of the Coruscant Prajii in this era were stereotyped as idle rich or career bureaucrats, a number did military service during the war: the [[Fort Praji|Kalandar Installation]] was renamed "Fort Praji" in the honor of [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Collin Praji]], and [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Praji (Moff)|Praji]] rose to command the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|GAR's]] [[Fourth Outer Rim Army]].<ref name="Tinker" /><ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

Following [[Operation Durge's Lance]], which saw Kaikielius [[Kaikielius campaign|conquered]] by the CIS, Tannon was forced to deal with refugees displaced from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] itself. Shortly afterwards, Palpatine [[Declaration of a New Order|declared]] the foundation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. In the new Imperial hierarchy, Tannon oversaw the transfer of prisoners from captured CIS worlds and the movement of transients into new construction projects. Maree and Onnelly Praji were resettled at the "[[Emerald Splendor Estates]]" on the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Byss/Legends|Byss]]. The relocation was nominally part of a much broader "recolonization effort" intended to attract the wealthy and powerful. In reality, the world was [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] private retreat. While there, Onnelly, Maree, and others like them were kept entertained, but unknown to them, Palpatine was secretly [[Force drain/Legends|draining]] their [[The Force/Legends|Force]] energy in order to sustain himself.<ref name="Tinker" />

===Later history===
Many of its members used their money and influence to enter into the higher-levels of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republican]] and [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] governments. The family donated a genetic [[Clone template/Legends|template]] for the Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] development program.

==Behind the scenes==
''[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji]]'' uses "Prajii" as the plural form of Praji.
